chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated, saying: Uthman ibn Muhammad and Abu Ya'qub al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf (dictated) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Shith narrated to us, saying: Asim ibn Abdullah al-Nakha'i narrated from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad from Sulayman al-Taymi from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi from Salman (may Allah be pleased with him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever prays four rak'at on the Day of Fitr (Eid al-Fitr) after the Imam's prayer, reciting 'Sabbihi Isma Rabbika al-A'la' (Glory be to the name of your Lord, the Most High) in the first, it is as if he has recited all the books, every book that Allah, Exalted and Mighty, revealed. And in the second rak'ah, 'Wa al-Shamsu wa duha-ha' (And the sun and its brightness), he receives a reward equal to what the sun shines upon. And in the third, 'Wa al-Duha' (And the morning hours), he receives a reward as if he has fed all the poor, anointed them, and cleansed them. And in the fourth, 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' (Say: He is Allah, the One) thirty times, Allah forgives him the sin of fifty years ahead and fifty years behind.

key_terms.سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى: Glory be to the name of your Lord, the Most High (Surah Al-A'la)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, the One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)
key_terms.وَالشَّمْسُ وَضُحَاهَا: And the sun and its brightness (Surah Al-Shams)

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for praying four rak'at on Eid al-Fitr after the Imam's prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on voluntary acts of worship (*nawafil*) to amplify the spiritual merit of Eid al-Fitr. The specific recitations correspond to the themes of divine glory, light, and monotheism, linking the prayer to the purification of the soul and the forgiveness of a century's worth of sins, reflecting the tradition's focus on detailed ritual rewards.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) says, “One who offers a four rakat  Salaat  after  Eid  congregational  prayer  reciting  Surah Aa’la in the first rakat it would be as if he has recited all the books revealed by Allah. If he recites Surah Shams in the second rakat he would get the reward equal to the number of things on which the rays of sun fall. If he recites Surah Zuha in the third rakat he would get the reward of feeding all the poor, cleaning and scenting them. If he recites Surah Tauheed ten times in the fourth rakat Allah would forgive the  sins committed by him during past and future fifty years.

Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ali, the writer of the book says that this reward is for the person who remained in Taqayyah and offered Salaat behind the Imam of other sect; then he should offer the above-mentioned Salaat with the intention of Eid prayer. One who prays behind an Imam appointed by Allah  whose  obedience  is  compulsory  cannot  offer  any Salaat till noon. If one offers Salaat behind an Imam of one’s own  sect  (whose  obedience  is  not  compulsory)  then  too there is no need to offer any Salaat till noon.
